decisions.reason: As a component line closely linked to the firm's drainage technology and customizable system architecture, it likely remains worth keeping unless several years of muted market response have clearly shown limited value.
Floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's stated strategic direction, so an established German specialist would usually continue it unless performance had become clearly disappointing.

Because this designer shower drainage line was framed as a flagship and fits the firm's design-conscious positioning, management would be reluctant to withdraw it after building market presence around it.
The integrated sloped shower element complements the broader shower installation solution and likely has option value as part of a system sale, so it would usually be retained.

This backflow-protected basement drain addresses a clear technical problem in a related niche, and for a long-established specialist the cost of keeping such a targeted line is likely modest relative to its portfolio value.

The air-admittance valve appears less central to the firm's shower-drainage-focused trajectory, so after several years management would be more likely to redeploy resources if demand had not proven strong.
